newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean leader says nation faces anarchy - report.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean leader says nation faces anarchy - report.

text.p: Anarchy could soon reign in North Korea because of an acute food shortage that has even hit the military, a leading South Korean newspaper on Wednesday quoted Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il as saying.
Kim held Communist Party and government officials responsible for "a state of anarchy being created because of food problems today," the Chosun Ilbo said.
Kim made the remarks in a speech on December 7 in Pyongyang, the daily said, without saying how it obtained the speech.
Chosun Ilbo, which is reputed to have many sources within the Seoul government, has published several scoops in recent months.
"People are found everywhere scrounging for food," Kim was quoted as saying. "Stations and trains are crowded with people looking for food. You see heartbreaking scenes everywhere."
Kim accused party officials of ignoring the plight of the people and doing "nothing but attending meetings and seminars".
"We are unable to supply enough food to the military," he was quoted as saying. "American imperialists will invade us immediately if they find out we cannot feed the military."
South Korean intelligence officials have said North Korea has given priority to its armed forces in allocating food.
Following two years of devastating floods, the Stalinst North has sought international food aid.
The United Nations' World Food Programme (WFP) said North Korea had a grain shortage of 2.3 million tonnes this year.

Catherine Bertini, WFP executive director, said on Tuesday at the end of a trip to North Korea that the presence of thin, lethargic children there indicated that a famine that could strike the impoverished state as early as this month.
Bertini said the WFP would start handing out 100,000 tonnes of grains and soybeans to farmers on April 1, with 20 percent of that going to children under the age of five.
